long_biography.plain_text:
Reading every client file in the William Morris Agency mailroom became Barry Diller's self-directed education in Hollywood. At ABC, the Movie of the Week established made-for-television films as a regular format. He later built Fox Broadcasting into a fourth national television network, a lasting challenge to the established broadcasters.

Creative production remained part of Diller's work beyond corporate management. His Broadway credits span productions such as The Humans and The Lehman Trilogy. Through the Diller-von Furstenberg Family Foundation, he also initiated Little Island after Hurricane Sandy damaged a Hudson River pier. The project became a public park designed to combine gardens, city views and live performance.
